claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you a few questions about Alex to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, attending school, college, or an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school anymore. He actually left education, but he has started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify one important detail:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship an apprenticeship in England specifically?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's not in England - he's doing his apprenticeship in Scotland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask a few more questions to complete my assessment:

**Are you currently living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Have you been receiving Child Benefit for Alex previously, or is this a new claim you're considering?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm looking to claim it - I want to know if I'm eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week in his apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working 24 hours or more a week.

conversation.text:
Good news! **You appear to be ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- Alex is 17 years old and lives with you in the UK
- While he has left education and started an apprenticeship, the rule that stops Child Benefit specifically applies to **apprenticeships in England only**
- Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Scotland, this exclusion doesn't apply to your situation
- Additionally, Alex is working less than 24 hours per week, so the rule about paid work stopping Child Benefit doesn't apply either

Since Alex is under 20, lives with you, and none of the disqualifying conditions apply to your circumstances, you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay back some or all of it through tax.

If you'd like to proceed with claiming, you can make a claim for Child Benefit through the official government channels.
